tagline: The people who run the grid, and the people who fund it.
sector: Invitation only annual executive summit for regional transmission operators, infrastructure investors and utility policy staff, produced by Meridian Council.
founded_place_size: Established 2016, produced from Providence, Rhode Island; one closed door summit a year, two days, eighteen seats.
about: Meridian Council runs a single invitation only summit each year for the small group that plans and pays for the electrical grid. It is deliberately intimate, closed door, and expensive, and everything a delegate touches at the venue is meant to feel like it cost what the seat cost. The summit works across three tracks, Operators who run the network, Capital who fund it, and Policy who regulate it.
audience: Eighteen delegates aged forty to sixty five who run regional transmission networks, sit on infrastructure funds or write utility policy, and have been to two hundred conferences already. For half the room the title is the reason they are in it.
price_positioning: Twenty four hundred dollars a seat, eighteen seats, invitation only. The register must read heavy, quiet and photo forward; anything bright or colour blocked reads as a name sticker at this price. Comparable commissions run 1,600 to 3,200 dollars fixed.
typography: A quiet, high contrast serif for the delegate name, set large and calm. A restrained sans in small caps for the organisation and the track distinction, carried as a typographic difference rather than a colour block. Generous space throughout, the portrait treated like a portrait.
voice: Spare and precise. We name who is in the room and why, and let the restraint do the talking. Example line the brand would write: 'Two days. Eighteen seats. A closed working session, not a stage.'
brand_assets_status: There is no working file for the badge; last year's was made by the venue's print bureau from artwork nobody kept. The only clean version of the summit mark that survives is the engraving on the brass lectern plate, photographed under the room's downlights. The registration board, the two session door cards and the closing slides do not exist yet.
values: Names and organisations exactly as registered, nothing shortened or abbreviated, and restraint carried as the signal of credibility.
